HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SAURABH BANERJEE  ORDER % 17.10.2023 1.

The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.399/2016 dated 05.07.2016 under Sections 498A/406/34 Indian Penal Code, 1860 [IPC], P.S. Sultan Puri, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom, in view of the fact that the parties have settled all their disputes amicably and are now living together.
2.
This petition is supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos.1 to 6 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
W.P.(CRL) 3050/2023 page 1 of 2
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/10/2023 at 23:55:42 5.
Learned ASC for the State accepts notice.
She confirms that she has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Respondent no.2 confirms that she has voluntarily settled all her disputes with the petitioners, of her own accord without any duress, coercion or pressure.

She further states that she does not wish to pursue the criminal proceedings against the petitioners and has no objection to the quashing of Jaivir Singh & Ors vs The State (N.C.T. Of Delhi) & Anr on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144929412/
1 the present FIR.

sentences.text:
7. In view of the fact that the disputes arise out of matrimonial discord and settlement has been arrived at between the parties, and as the respondent no.2 does not wish to continue with the criminal proceedings, in order to bring a quietus to the present disputes and for the well being of the children and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi &
Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
